{{Short description|Form of reasoning – not either/or}}
{{Redirect|Both/And|the anthology|Both/And: Essays by Trans and Gender-Nonconforming Writers of Color|the memoir|Both/And: A Life in Many Worlds}}
{{Orphan|date=January 2024}}
'''Both/and''' is an [[Academy|academic]] concept which refers to a form of reasoning which resists [[Binary thinking|binary]] or [[False dilemma|either/or]] styles of thinking.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Strawser |first=Michael |title=Both/And: Reading Kierkegaard- From Irony to Edification |date=1996-12-31 |publisher=Fordham University Press |isbn=978-0-8232-9519-7 |doi=10.1515/9780823295197}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Bell |first=Jeffrey A. |title=Philosophy at the edge of chaos: Gilles Deleuze and the philosophy of difference |date=2006 |publisher=University of Toronto press |isbn=978-0-8020-9409-4 |series=Toronto Studies in Philosophy |location=Toronto }}</ref>

Unlike dualistic styles of reasoning, both/and means that between two options, both can be valid, or that their opposition may present opportunities for [[dialectic]]al synthesis, rather than a complete rejection of one of the premises in favor of the other.

Both/and is associated with dialectical thinking, which means investigating contradictions in order to attain higher understanding. However, it also appears in broader systems of thought, such as the concept of [[nondualism]], in which the distinction between self and other is transcended.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Potter |first1=Karl H. |last2=Loy |first2=David |date=1991 |title=Nonduality. A Study in Comparative Philosophy |journal=Philosophy and Phenomenological Research |volume=51 |issue=3 |pages=733 |doi=10.2307/2107905 |jstor=2107905 |issn=0031-8205}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Griebel |first=Oliver |date=2019 |title=Nonduality-Non/duality-Many-One Duality |journal=Integral Review: A Transdisciplinary & Transcultural Journal for New Thought, Research, & Praxis |volume=15 |issue=1}}</ref>

The term has been used in a texts on [[Business management|management]], [[literary theory]], classroom research, [[religious studies]], [[methodology]], and [[international relations]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Smith |first1=Wendy K. |author-link1=Wendy K. Smith |title=Both/and thinking: embracing creative tensions to solve your toughest problems |last2=Lewis |first2=Marianne W. |author-link2=Marianne W. Lewis |date=2022 |publisher=Harvard Business Review Press |isbn=978-1-64782-104-3 |location=Boston, Massachusetts}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Friedman |first=Susan Stanford |date=2017 |title=Both/And: Critique and Discovery in the Humanities |journal=Publications of the Modern Language Association of America |language=en |volume=132 |issue=2 |pages=344–351 |doi=10.1632/pmla.2017.132.2.344 |s2cid=148781703 |issn=0030-8129}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Andermahr |first=Sonya |date=2018-09-15 |title=Both/And Aesthetics: Gender, Art, and Language in Brigid Brophy's In Transit and Ali Smith's How to Be Both |journal=Contemporary Women's Writing |language=en |volume=12 |issue=2 |pages=248–263 |doi=10.1093/cww/vpy001 |issn=1754-1476}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Casile |first1=Maureen |last2=Hoover |first2=Kristine F. |last3=O'Neil |first3=Deborah A. |date=2011-03-15 |editor-last=Millican |editor-first=Juliet |title=Both-and, not either-or: knowledge and service-learning |journal=Education + Training |language=en |volume=53 |issue=2/3 |pages=129–139 |doi=10.1108/00400911111115672 |issn=0040-0912}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |chapter=The Secular Sacred: In between or both/and? |date=2016-04-01 |title=Social Identities Between the Sacred and the Secular |pages=163–178 |publisher=Routledge|doi=10.4324/9781315609454-20 |doi-broken-date=11 July 2025 |isbn=978-1-315-60945-4 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Probst |first=Barbara |date=2016-03-08 |title=Both/and: researcher as participant in qualitative inquiry |journal=Qualitative Research Journal |volume=16 |issue=2 |doi=10.1108/qrj-06-2015-0038 |issn=1443-9883}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ovadia |first=Jesse Salah |date=2013 |title=Accumulation with or without dispossession?
